text:
alex: quick question — is anyone thinking about "prompt-aware micro-warmup" for cold-starts? low-latency use-cases (chat widgets) where we only need first few kv layers hot. :thinking:
priya: yup, i've been noodling on a design that uses a tiny set of representative prefixes to drive selective shard prefetch. idea: fingerprint incoming prompt, map to a warmup-profile that lists which layers/chunks are hot for that pattern.
jamie: curious about privacy — storing fingerprints of customer prompts could be tricky for regulated customers. can we do this without retaining raw prompts?\alex: totally — the plan is to store only hashed fingerprints + an aggregate hotness vector, not the prompt text. nothing PII.
yousef: tradeoffs: saves IO at cold start but adds complexity to manifest and routing. also risk of wrong profile causing extra latency if we prefetch the wrong blocks.
priya: mitigation: fall back to a fast zero-copy index-first read for the immediate tokens and concurrently warm up additional layers async. micro-warmup is only to avoid the first interleaved small-request spike.
jamie: can you sketch the manifest changes? post a minimal example pls.
priya: sure — thinking of adding an optional `warmup_profiles` field in the bundle manifest: it maps fingerprint buckets -> list of (shard, layer-range, priority). e.g.
```json
"warmup_profiles": {
  "sha256:a3f4...": [
    {"shard": 2, "layers": "0-5", "priority": "high"},
    {"shard": 7, "layers": "6-8", "priority": "low"}
  ]
}
```
yousef: how would the runtime use that without blocking inference? We should define a `warmup_hint` header so the router can tell the daemon what to prefetch.
alex: proposal: add an optional header `Warmup-Hint: fp=sha256:...;prefetch=shard:2:layers=0-5;mode=micro` — runtime checks local cache, fetches high-priority blocks with best-effort and runs inference using index-first for anything missing.
jamie: that header looks fine but watch for header length limits if we encode too much. maybe encode as short IDs and keep profiles in the registry.
priya: good point. store profiles server-side, only send `Warmup-Fingerprint` header. runtime does a small lookup to registry if allowed. for private deployments, registry can be local.
yousef: instrumentation: we need telemetry: warmup_match (hit/miss), warmup_latency_savings, extra_bytes_prefetched, and a privacy flag if profile was from aggregated public dataset.
priya: +1. also need an opt-out per-customer config. enterprise tenants sometimes don't want even hashed signals.
ajex: (typo) alex: action items?
priya: i can draft an RFC with the manifest schema and header shape. jamie — can you validate compliance/privacy wording? yousef — can you estimate perf delta and implementation effort for runtime?
jamie: will do, i can check with legal on the hashed fingerprint retention policy.
yousef: quick back-of-envelope: micro-warmup should shave 20-40ms on median cold-requests for chat flows that only need first 6 layers, but io overhead might increase cost by ~1-3% from extra small-file fetches. need experiments.
infra-bot: deploy queued: warmup-profiles-registry v0.1 -> staging (depends: none) :truck:
priya: ok i'll put a toy PoC in `eng-ml/warmup-poc` and the RFC draft in Notion. keeping it conservative: warmup only for profiles with > 2x observed savings in telemetry.
jamie: sounds reasonable. thanks all. :thumbsup:
